candidates.source_name: TED — Tenders Electronic Daily (EU Official Journal Supplement)
candidates.why_relevant: Publishes EU-institution and EU-external-action contract and award notices, including EU Delegation to North Macedonia procurements and IPA/EU-funded service contracts. Award notices name winning vendors and contract values, which is the single richest supranational signal for who supplies MK banking/payments-adjacent IT and consultancy.
candidates.access_status: public, free; search UI plus notice PDFs; bulk/API access documented
candidates.legal_status: EU open data / re-use permitted under EU Commission re-use decision
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use TED search API / expert query with country=MK and CPV codes for financial IT (72xxx, 66xxx, 30144/30233 card & payment hardware); schedule daily delta pull of new notices; archive notice PDFs.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from EU procurement result pages
queries_used: TED tenders electronic daily North Macedonia banking payment system tender notice

candidates.suggested_collection_method: Follow procurement-detail permalinks discovered via TED/site search; scrape record fields (buyer, CPV, value, status) at low rate.

negative_findings.description: UN Development Business (devbusiness.un.org), historically the mandatory publication venue for World Bank General Procurement Notices, phased down and ceased activity on its website on 31 March 2025.
negative_findings.result_summary: Legacy GPN pages still resolve, but the platform is no longer a live feed; WB procurement plans that cite 'publication in UNDB' now effectively route through STEP and the WB external site.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collector built on UNDB would silently go stale; the GPN channel for MK WB projects must be re-pointed to the World Bank projects/procurement pages.

negative_findings.description: No specific TED notice for a North Macedonia banking or payment-system procurement was surfaced through general web search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search returned TED platform/meta pages and unrelated MK notices (insurance, events, road transport) rather than a payments-sector notice.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that TED must be queried through its own expert search/API with country and CPV filters rather than via general web search; absence here is a search-method limitation, not evidence that no such notices exist.

negative_findings.description: No IFC-specific procurement or advisory-tender channel for North Macedonia financial sector was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: IFC did not appear in any of the donor-procurement searches run; IFC advisory engagements are typically not tendered publicly in the way IBRD/EBRD project procurement is.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: IFC was named in the cell scope; its low public-procurement footprint should be recorded so the cell is not treated as incomplete, but IFC disclosure portals still need a dedicated pass.

negative_findings.description: No Macedonian-language donor procurement portal exists for EBRD, World Bank, UNDP or KfW notices — all publish in English only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Macedonian-language searching productively found the national/IPA side (CFCD, СЕП, МЕП, Министерство за финансии) but returned no MK-language IFI notice source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The MK-language layer of this cell is inherently limited to the national IPA structures; collectors must not expect MK text from the IFI side, and analysts should not read the absence of MK notices as absence of activity.

negative_findings.description: DevelopmentAid tender records for MK donor tenders are gated behind a paid membership.
negative_findings.result_summary: Tender view pages render title, donor, sector and status but withhold the notice body and documents without a subscription.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Useful as a discovery index only; evidence-grade collection must go back to the originating donor portal.

negative_findings.description: ECEPP, UNGM and e-nabavki.gov.mk were identified from search results and documentation rather than fetched; their crawlability is a hypothesis.
negative_findings.result_summary: All three are known to be JS-heavy and/or registration-gated; no fetch was attempted in this pass, so no liveness or blocking claim is made.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design for these three should budget for headless browsing or account-based alerting; a later verification pass must confirm.

coverage_gaps.description: IFC, MIGA and the Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB) were not covered; CEB in particular lends to Western Balkan financial intermediaries.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass over IFC disclosure/advisory pages, MIGA project briefs and coebank.org project and procurement pages filtered on North Macedonia.

coverage_gaps.description: Bilateral donors active in MK financial-sector/digitalisation work — SECO/Swiss cooperation, GIZ/BMZ, Sida, USAID successor arrangements, and Austrian/Dutch bilateral programmes — were not individually enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each bilateral donor, locate its MK country page and its procurement/tender channel (GIZ's own tender portal, SECO's public listings, embassy calls) and record them as separate candidates.

coverage_gaps.description: Award-side transparency registers were only partially covered: the EU Financial Transparency System (FTS) and the EC's beneficiary/contractor listings were not examined.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add EU FTS and the Commission's annual list of contracts awarded, filtered on MK-resident and MK-delivering contractors, to capture awards that never reach TED.

coverage_gaps.description: No CPV / UNSPSC code list has been fixed for banking and payments procurement, so all searching in this cell is still keyword-based and lossy.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define the code set (e.g. CPV 66100000 banking, 72200000/72500000 software and IT services, 30144200 ticket/card machines, 30233xxx card readers) and drive TED/OpenTender queries from codes rather than words.

coverage_gaps.description: Macedonian searching used Cyrillic only; Albanian-language MK sources and Latin-script Macedonian transliterations were not tried.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Repeat key queries in Albanian ('tenderë', 'prokurim publik', 'IPA') and in Latin-script Macedonian ('javni nabavki', 'tenderi') to catch mirrored institutional content.

coverage_gaps.description: Historic donor award records (pre-2020 IPA II, closed EBRD/WB operations) were not systematically located; CFCD content is split between a live and an archive host.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Crawl arhiva-cfcd.finance.gov.mk and arhiva.finance.gov.mk in full, and pull closed-project contract awards from the WB Socrata dataset, to build a multi-year vendor baseline.

brief: Supranational and donor-funded procurement touching MK banking and payments runs through three distinct, non-overlapping layers: EU channels (TED, the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, EEAS Delegation Skopje, and nationally the CFCD in the Ministry of Finance, which is the sole IPA contracting authority under indirect management), IFI channels (EBRD's ECEPP, World Bank procurement plans plus the Socrata contract-awards dataset and WB corporate RFXs such as the explicitly payments-focused 'Electronic Payments in North Macedonia' assignment with the National Bank), and UN/bilateral channels (UNDP notices, UNGM, KfW-financed fund management units). Award-level vendor names are most reliably obtained from the World Bank contract-awards dataset, EBRD contract-award notices, and CFCD's contracted-projects listing, while procurement plans and donor policy briefs give six-to-eighteen months of forward warning before any notice appears. Macedonian-language search is productive only on the national IPA side (ЦФСД, СЕП, МЕП, Министерство за финансии) — every IFI publishes in English only, and donor-funded lots following the national market approach are diverted to e-nabavki.gov.mk, so the cell cannot be collected completely without a hand-off to the national-portal cell. Main residual risks are the retirement of UN Development Business as a GPN venue, registration/JS gating on ECEPP, UNGM and e-nabavki, and the absence of a fixed CPV code set to replace keyword search.
